newsitem.title: CONGO: Congo Brazzaville government denounces coup bid.
newsitem.headline: Congo Brazzaville government denounces coup bid.

text.p: Congo Brazzaville's government said on Sunday that former president Denis Sassou Nguesso was trying to stage a coup and urged the population to support the security forces.

The government made the accusation in a statement read on national radio after four days of heavy fighting between troops loyal to President Pascal Lissouba, militia allies and militia loyal to Sassou Nguesso in the capital of the former French colony.

"Following the operations to maintain order... the government informs national and international opinion that it's a question of a coup attempt by Denis Sassou Nguesso who once again wants to take power by force of arms," it said in a statement on national radio.

"The government thanks the security forces for the determination to bar the way of the attackers. The government asks the Congolese people to stay vigilant and support the security forces to save our young democracy."
A spokesman for Sassou Nguesso said earlier that they were not trying to topple Lissouba, who won election in 1992, and that they were simply defending themselves from attack.
The standoff between the two men and their supporters or political or ethnic allies broke out during a tense run-up to a presidential election scheduled for July 27.
